757 Monday evening, [15 October 1798 postmark]
WILLIAM DRENNAN, [DUBLIN], TO MARTHA MCTIER, BELFAST [722]
Dear Matty, I have not written to you, because I have not been in a humour to say
nothing, and as for making news of any kind, it has been long over with me. Shall
I tell you, that Mrs Daniel has not yet been brought to bed; that Mrs Orr and
Robert and his brothers are well; that Holmes calls here as usual, and Armstrong;
that Sampson had gone on board for Portugal, but I believe has returned having
been taken so ill as to vomit blood; that nothing as yet is determined finally with
respect to the other prisoners (who you may suppose will not take my romantically
prudent advice of emigrating in corps to Madel[i]ra, or even to Ithaca, if it were not
a French possession); that I received a large fee from Miss S[mith] which after a
great many delicacies bandied about, I, as you may expect, put into my pocket; that
I wrote to my London friend'” once and again, and sent him some paper which
how he will use I know not; that Burrough after having had his house so long unset,
was offered £85 per annum by an attorney who met him in the street, with which
offer he instantly closed, and I see the present proprietor is repairing it already to
his taste; that therefore I stay for the present where I am, and will I suppose con-
tinue here, as there appears no probability of your being able to dispose of your
house even for the winter months.
I was looking a day or two ago at a house in Cumberland Street, immediately
opposite to David Gordon's, very convenient, with two parlours, two drawing
rooms, and a coach-house and stables nicely fitted up for four horses (which might
be let for 15 guineas at the least), and the present proprietor Mrs Jocelyn," widow
of the late Mr Jocelyn, a brother of the Surveyor in Belfast, asks for this very good
but not very large house 50 guineas a year and £300 fine, the taxes low. I asked Mr
Metge'“ who is appointed to let the house whether the fine could be lessened and
the rent increased, but he was not inclined to do that, at the same time mentioning
his desire to give me a preference, or to mention to me any other proposal before
he closed with it.
The report of an union will not have any immediate effect on the price of houses,
though I think it will reduce a good deal the value of men in this country. It is said,
